metadata.blog_title: Times 29431 – Just right! – Times for The Times

across.clue_text: Cross about Scottish inventor being guest announcer (8)
across.wordplay: ROOD backwards + [Alexander Graham] BELL.   I’ll admit, the literal got me.

across.clue_text: Computer part used in US city work (6)

across.wordplay: Anagram of THAT FRAME, for a word that should be fresh in everyone’s mind.

across.clue_text: Ocean feature ruined at the outset, covered in fuel (5)
Republican backing vote for quite some time? (4)
What may indicate rest of Hampshire region? (3,6)
across.wordplay: Reverse cryptic, where NEW FOREST might be used to clue REST OF.

across.clue_text: Completely exhausted, given ovation on departure? (7-3)
Hard avoiding the children in college (4)
Standard reference point? We align uneasily (4,6)
Weakened terms in lease when payment ran out (9)
across.wordplay: [leas]E [whe]N + FEE + BLED.   The use of term for last letter seems to have jumped from Mephisto into the daily.
B(A)P’S, British Petroleum, a company I have owned several times.

across.clue_text: Soldiers excessively quiet when crossing furthest part of border (5)
Revised recent idea, not needing America to act as peacemaker (9)
Advanced source of entertainment I found in the French country (6)
across.wordplay: L(A,TV,I)A.   A complex cryptic with a lot of ways to go wrong.

across.clue_text: This reduced each example of criminal behaviour (8)

down.clue_text: Film at sea, perhaps type to include river (2,3,10)
down.wordplay: ON THE WATER + F(R)ONT.   Undoubtedly biffed by many solvers.

down.clue_text: Data presentation showing reduction initially in pub opening hours (3,5)
Component of basic education adopted by spare master (5)
TV host’s job curtailed after article (6)
Retired copper with personnel in support restrain New York man (10,5)
down.wordplay: T(HR)EE + PEN + NY + PIECE.   Those looking for CU backwards will be sadly disappointed.

down.clue_text: Sea creature: plan to net one going over western sound (5,5)
down.wordplay: P(I)LOT + W + HALE.   The palin whale does not exist!

down.clue_text: Question posed in shock English musical number (4,4)
Possibly flat account: the same, though not in charge (10)
down.wordplay: ACC + IDENT[ic]AL.   You’ll have to ask the chatbot if acc. is a valid abbreviation for account.   It’s a flat in musical notation we’re talking about here.

down.clue_text: One’s boring regular practice took effect (5,3)
Flying ace destined to be consumed by anger (8)
Upturn in illumination with Greek character here? (6)
down.definition: Upturn in illumination with Greek character here?
down.wordplay: LED upside-down + PHI.   Since Delphi was the site of an oracle, presumably our Greek friend found the light here.
D[iver’s] + ITCH.  One of the few easy clues in this puzzle.

down.clue_text: Refuse to accept study on undetermined quantity (4)
down.wordplay: DEN + Y.   Another of the same – the setter seems to have run out of novel ideas.
